dedupe_keys.name: bezpy geomagnetic geoelectric and impedance analysis in python

description: bezpy is an open-source Python library for analysing geomagnetic (B), geoelectric (E) and magnetotelluric impedance (Z) data, used to estimate how geomagnetic storms induce electric fields and voltages on power transmission lines. It calculates the geoelectric field from the geomagnetic field in several ways and integrates that field along transmission lines, with tutorials for storm maps, storm catalogues, continuous scans to hazard maps, line voltages and gridded impedance, plus a reproducibility guide mapping published papers to the current interface. It is written by Greg M. Lucas with contributors and builds on pandas, NumPy and SciPy. The method is location-independent; examples include the Halloween 2003 storm in Japan and North China impedance data. Version 0.2.0 (August 2026) is on GitHub and Zenodo under the MIT licence at no cost and needs Python 3.12 or later. Caveats: version 0.2.0 fixed Delaunay interpolation weights, so line voltages computed that way change by a few percent against published 2019 and 2020 workflows, and results depend on the quality of impedance data. Simulation uses are space weather hazard exposure and resilience assessment of transmission grids against geomagnetically induced currents.
